Purpose and exclusions

Use one Gameplay Ability System stack for health, mana, stamina, abilities, costs, cooldowns and effects. A player's ASC lives on PlayerState during one zone session; the current body is its avatar. An ordinary enemy owns its ASC on its Character.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Enable Gameplay Ability System and Gameplay Tags dependencies in the C++ project. Add the needed GameplayAbilities, GameplayTags and GameplayTasks module dependencies using the installed engine conventions.
  2. Define URPGAttributeSet and URPGAbilitySystemComponent; PlayerState owns both and the Character implements IAbilitySystemInterface by returning that same ASC. Do not add another player ASC to the pawn.
  3. Create DA_CombatRules_Default and the initial GE_DefaultAttributes, GE_Damage, GE_Healing, GE_Cost and GE_Cooldown assets from their intended GAS bases. Separate authored effects from live active-effect state.
  4. Implement server possession and owning-client replicated-PlayerState readiness hooks. Check InitAbilityActorInfo and related API signatures in the installed 5.8.3 headers before compiling.
  5. Configure owner/public effect replication deliberately and measure PlayerState update rates; a common mixed-mode choice is only adopted after its owner-chain requirements are verified.
  6. Reopen BP_PlayerCharacter movement adapters to consume the ASC's stamina; reopen WBP_HUD and WBP_ActionBar to bind attribute/cooldown delegates and display server rejection text.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in GAS ownership, attributes, costs and prediction. Rule owner: URPGAbilitySystemComponent. This asset’s role is Use one Gameplay Ability System stack for health, mana, stamina, abilities, costs, cooldowns and effects. A player's ASC lives on PlayerState during one zone session; the current body is its avatar. An ordinary enemy owns its ASC on its Character.

  1. On server possession, obtain the PlayerState ASC, validate hydrated build, initialize actor info with PlayerState as owner and Character as avatar, then apply default attributes and granted abilities once.
  2. On the owning client, PlayerState replication and possession readiness both call one guarded initialization path. Do not assume BeginPlay/OnRep order; rebind after respawn and clear old avatar delegates.
  3. Input tags resolve to granted ability specs. Use supported GAS local prediction for responsiveness, while the server rechecks costs, tags, target/range/LOS and cooldown.
  4. Server commits accepted GAS cost/cooldown and applies effects. Rejected predictions are reconciled by GAS and the project's UI/visual observer; never maintain a second manually predicted health balance.
  5. ASC delegates produce read-only attribute updates and semantic action cues for PaperZD; no PlayMontageAndWait dependency is assumed for sprites.
  6. On death cancel transient abilities and reinitialize the new avatar; on cross-server transfer create a new ASC and rebuild from durable definition IDs, not serialized object pointers/spec handles. Persist selected long cooldown expiries under a declared policy.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_NetworkLab / Character_A / Enemy_Dummy. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Respawn twice -> exactly one ability grant set and one set of UI delegates.
Predicted cast with insufficient server mana -> rejection restores local presentation/cost expectation; no enemy damage.
PlayerState arrives after pawn -> HUD waits, then binds once; no null ASC access.
Zone transfer during cast -> cast canceled; a long cooldown does not reset merely because a new ASC is created.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
